main_text.p: competitores existebant, & iudicio ar-chontis utplurimum definiebantur,aut ab eo ad iudicia superiora referebantur.

Quam ob causam eædem puellæ aut fœminæ etiam ἐπίδικοι[?], quòd iudicio de iis certaretur, dicebantur. Quòd si pupillæ hujusmodi inopes essent, cogebantur nihilominus sanguine proximi eas uxores ducere, aut de suo dotem fortunæ congruam, iis dare. Nec deerat iisdem respubl. si hoc quoque subsidio forte destituerentur, nimirum si ipsi propinqui egeni essent, modò ipsæ formæ essent mediocris, ne ob ejus defectum nuptiis fastidirentur.

Quod argumentum Demosthenis verba contra Neæram. Ait enim, judices appellans: Quapropter & civium nostrarum rationem habete, ut ne pauperum filiæ nuptum collocari nequeant. Nunc enim tametsi aliqua pauperCula est, dotem ei satis magnam confert lex, si mediocrem duntaxat a natura formam acceperit. Vnde verò stipendia hæc in paupercularum dotes respub. sumpserit, ex pretio-ne vendi-torum scortorum, an mulcta alia impudicorum, incertum. Illud quidem verba Demosthenis hoc eodem loco significare videntur. Nifi forte toto isto loco orator legem eam intelligat, qua proximus agnatus jubetur pro facultatum

page.notes: Uncertain readings: the Greek word ἐπίδικοι is marked [?]. "pauperCula" is printed with a capital C and is kept as printed. Line 16 "Demosthenis" and the start of the line after "Quod ar-" are partly overprinted by red marks and the left-margin signs, so the exact wording there is doubtful; I read it as printed but it is not certain. The left-margin marks beside lines 15 to 31 are too faint or overprinted to read as notes, so none are transcribed. The running head and page number are printed at the top. Catchword "tum" is printed at the lower right.
